thread.title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Lower as Lackluster Manufacturing Data, Apple's Lower Sales Outlook Fuel Slump

author: MT Newswires
title: Mid-Day ETF Update: ETFs, Stocks Lower as Lackluster Manufacturing Data, Apple's Lower Sales Outlook Fuel Slump
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds in Thursday's regular session:
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): -1.2%
ProShares UltraPro Short QQQ ( SQQQ ): +5.8%
Invesco QQQ Trust, Series 1 ( QQQ ): -1.9%
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): -1.4%
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ): -1.1%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including IWM and IVV were lower. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ ( QQQ ) was down 0.3%.
US stocks extended their losses, weighed down by a sales warning from Apple (AAPL) and amplified later in the morning by economic data that triggered fears of a recession.
Selling erupted after Apple slashed its Q1 revenue guidance on Wednesday after the close below Wall Street's expectations, citing the US-China trade war, economic weakness in emerging markets and headwinds from the stronger dollar. Shares of the tech giant fell to their lowest level in 18 months, shorting out the Nasdaq's five-session winning streak.
Selling was briefly suspended on dovish remarks from the president of the Dallas Fed and a rebound in the dollar but quickly returned after the December ISM manufacturing index slid to its lowest level in two-years, coming on the heels of a 15-month low in the comparable manufacturing PMI. Nearly every subindex was down in December with new orders plunging to 51.1 from November's 62.1, and the price index falling to 54.9 from 60.7.
This morning's other data included a greater-than-expected increase of 10,000 in initial jobless claims while the private sector created 271,000 new jobs in December, exceeding expectations for a 175,000 gain.
Power Play: Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) was down 1.2%, while other health care funds including Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Healthcare (IYH) were lower. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was up 1.5%.
Bristol-Myers Squibb Company (BMY) has agreed to buy Celgene (CELG) for about $74 billion. Celgene shareholders will receive one share of Bristol-Myers and $50 in cash for each Celgene share they own. They also will receive one tradeable contingent value right for each share of Celgene they own, entitling them to a payment for the achievement of future regulatory milestones.
Winners and Losers
Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was down 1.3%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was down 2.5% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was up 2.4%.
PCSB Financial (PCSB) rose marginally after it said late Wednesday that PCSB Bank completed its conversion to a New York-chartered commercial bank from a New York-chartered savings bank. Following the conversion, PCSB Commercial Bank, a wholly owned subsidiary of PCSB Bank, merged with and into PCSB Bank, resulting in PCSB Bank as the surviving institution.
Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) was down 3.7%, while tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW) and iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) were in the red.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) was down 4.2% and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) was down 4.6%.
FTE Networks (FTNW) were up more than 6% after the company said it closed 2018 with $572.4 million in new contract awards, with about $129.6 million new infrastructure projects secured in Q4. According to FTE, the contract awards cover infrastructure projects primarily in New York and surrounding boroughs. Work associated with the new projects is expected to be completed within the next 12 to 18 months.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was down 0.1% and Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was down 0.1%.
Sempra Energy (SRE) rose 1% after it said late Wednesday that its subsidiary has entered into an agreement to sell its non-utility U.S. natural gas storage facilities to an affiliate of ArcLight Capital Partners for $332 million in cash, subject to adjustments for working capital.
Commodities
Crude was up 0.3%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was up 0.1%. Natural gas down 0.8% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was down 0.8%.
Gold was down 0.2%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was up 0.6%. Silver was up 0.5%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was up 1.2%.
Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) was up 0.3% and Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones U.S. Consumer Goods (IYK) were lower.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) was down 1.1% while retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were firmer.
Toyota Motor (TM) fell 1% after it reported that it sold 220,910 vehicles in North America in December, a decline of 0.9% from a year ago, beating industry estimates for a decline of 1.3%. By model, Camry was the best-selling car in its segment in 2018 with 29,093 cars sold in December, while 25,439 Corollas were sold last month. The RAV4 had its best December on record with an 18.8% increase in sales while 4Runner sales were up 11.3%. Sales of pickup trucks were also strong as Tacoma sales were up 15.1% and Tundra sales rose 3.0% in December.
